Evidence was heard that 2 separate community pharmacists did not tell Lyn, (nor pass a message via her family who collected the tablets), that she must stop taking simvastatin during the course of the clarithromycin, required for her chest infection. The pharmacists did not know she was taking simvastatin. I am concerned that there is confusion and a variety of opinion amongst community pharmacists around the extent of the expectation or duty to perform 'clinical checks' to enable safe prescribing and what that practically entails.
lack of clinical checks by community pharmacists



I am concerned that there is confusion amongst community pharmacists in Wales around the conflict between the expectation of safe prescribing/dispensing and patient confidentiality (when someone other than the patient collects the medication).
conflict between safe prescribing/dispensing and patient confidentiality



I am concerned that community pharmacists in Wales only have very limited access to the Welsh Clinical Portal, where they can see relevant drug history and recent test results, which would enable them to properly and safely counsel patients to stop contraindicated drugs (here simvastatin with clarithromycin) but applicable more widely. I heard evidence that access to such information is available routinely in English pharmacies, but only in exceptional circumstances in Wales. I have no understanding of why that is the case.
limited access to Welsh Clinical Portal



Here, had either community pharmacist had access to Lyn's drug history, they would have noted the contraindication and either told Lyn, her representative or written on the pharmacy bag that she was to stop the simvastatin. This likely would have changed the outcome for Lyn.
missed opportunity to prevent contraindication
